en: Dependent on an indeterminate (abyākata) dhamma that is impinging (sappaṭigha), an unwholesome (na-kusala) dhamma that is non-impinging (na-sappaṭigha) arises by way of root-condition (hetu-paccaya).
Dependent on an indeterminate dhamma that is impinging, an unwholesome dhamma that is non-impinging arises by way of root-condition.
Dependent on an indeterminate dhamma that is impinging, [both] an unwholesome dhamma that is non-impinging and a neither-wholesome-nor-unwholesome dhamma that is non-impinging [arise]...
And states arise by way of the root condition. Under the root [condition], there are three; ... pe ... under non-disappearance, there are three.
Wholesome with non-reactive [states] has three; unwholesome with non-reactive has three; indeterminate with non-reactive has three.
Wholesome with non-reactive and indeterminate with non-reactive has three; unwholesome with non-reactive and indeterminate...

And non-reactive [states] are three. With respect to root-cause, there are fifteen ... pe ... with respect to mutuality, three ... pe ... with respect to result, three ... pe ... with respect to non-disappearance, fifteen.
